# Grothendieck–Teichmüller Conjecture

Status Open LLM status Open unverified

## Statement

### Definitions and mathematical statement

Let $\widehat F_2$ be the free profinite group on $x,y$, and let $\chi:G_{{\mathbb{Q}}}\to\widehat{{\mathbb{Z}}}^\times$ be the cyclotomic character. Drinfeld's original $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ consists of the compatible invertible profinite pairs satisfying the commutator, symmetry, hexagon, and pentagon conditions; all these conditions, not only the pair equations, are incorporated from the source. Under the fixed Ihara splitting, \[ \mathrm{Ih}(g)=\left((\chi(g)-1)/2,f_g\right),\qquad x\mapsto x^{\chi(g)},\quad y\mapsto f_g^{-1}y^{\chi(g)}f_g. \] The question is surjectivity of this actual embedding $G_{{\mathbb{Q}}}\hookrightarrow\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. Gentle, pro-$\ell$, and prounipotent groups are not substituted. Composition and coordinate conventions must agree with Section 1.3 of the cited paper.

Formulation and concept references: [S1].

### Short English statement

Is every symmetry in the original profinite Grothendieck--Teichmüller group induced by a unique automorphism of the algebraic closure of the rationals?

### Sources

  * S1 Ivan Bortnovskyi, Vasily A. Dolgushev, Borys Holikov, Vadym Pashkovskyi, Accessing non-abelian quotients of the Grothendieck-Teichmueller group via elementary tools, arXiv2405.11725v3,6August2026,35pages. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.11725v3. Formulation source. Consulted 24 September 2026: Section 1.3, equations (1.5)--(1.6).
  * S2 Accessing non-abelian quotients of the Grothendieck-Teichmueller group via elementary tools. https://arxiv.org/html/2405.11725. Further reference; not a proof endorsement.
  * S3 Galois actions on surfaces and a higher genus Grothendieck-Teichmüller group. https://arxiv.org/html/2606.01466v1. Further reference; not a proof endorsement.
  * S4 Proving the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Conjecture for Profinite Spaces & The Galois Grothendieck Path Integral. https://arxiv.org/html/2503.13006. Further reference; not a proof endorsement.

The conjecture asserts that this actual continuous injective homomorphism is surjective, hence an isomorphism of profinite groups. The source's group law and fixed splitting are retained; formulas from an opposite composition convention are not mixed into this definition.

### Why it matters

Surjectivity would identify that entire profinite group with the arithmetic Galois group through the actual embedding. Failure would exhibit elements satisfying the group’s defining conditions that do not arise from Galois symmetries.

### Status

Open

Grothendieck–Teichmuller remains open for surjectivity of the fixed Ihara embedding into the original full profinite GT. August 2026 quotient results and underlying-space homeomorphisms do not prove this group-homomorphism surjectivity.

Status reviewed Sep 14, 2026

For the role of dimensions 1 and 2, going through the boundary of the $\overline M_{g,\nu}$, he finds four elementary cases ($\overline M_{0,4}$, $\overline M_{1,1}$, $\overline M_{0,5}$, $\overline M_{1,2}$) and has the impression that understanding them will give the key ("donnera la clef") to the rest (see folder 147, p. 59). Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps proved the discrete version of this (Crelle 521, 2000).

Later work

  * Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki showed that $\widehat{GT}\times S_{m+3}\simeq\mathrm{Out}(\widehat\Gamma_{0,m+3})$, so $\widehat{GT}$ is a purely group-theoretic object (Kodai Math. J. 45, 2022),

  * Hoshi, Mochizuki and Tsujimura rebuilt $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ from subgroups of $\widehat{GT}$ that are compatible with all Belyi diagrams (J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 32, 2025),

  * Collas suggests a group defined through Belyi maps as a candidate for $G_{\mathbb Q}$ (arXiv:2603.02848, §4.3.3, 2026).

  * For part (2) of the question, an OpenAI preprint claims a proof of the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture, with a Lean formalisation of the main statement. (OpenAI, September 2026, not refereed)

Whether $G_{\mathbb Q}\simeq\widehat{GT}$ is still open.

We prove a presentation theorem for maps out of $\mathbf{S}$ using genus-zero and genus-one generators and relations.
